interface.title: Flood-Net (ALERT flood-warning telemetry network planner)
interface.field: Hydrology / flood-warning radio telemetry engineering (ALERT rain and river gauges, VHF repeaters)
interface.stage_of_work: Network planning, radio-path checks and checking logger data for a running gauge network
interface.what_it_is_for: Engineers browse a network of about 4,900 flood-warning stations and 146 repeaters on a map, see which repeaters carry which station addresses, check radio paths with terrain profiles and Longley-Rice link budgets, and import logger CSV exports to filter and chart rainfall time series.

data.source: Station and repeater data bundled with the app (stations.json); only the two logger CSVs on the Plots tab were uploaded test files
data.note: The station and repeater dataset loaded by itself from the bundled stations.json (banner: '4947 stations · 146 repeaters · from stations.json (this site)'). The live Supabase datastore could not be reached, so health, 'last heard' and the on-air receptions show 'Failed to fetch'. Basemap tiles did not render (grey background), but pins, rivers, links and terrain elevation for the profiles did load. On the Plots tab I uploaded both test CSVs (Durikai AL rainfall 541134 and Tyalgum Bridge rainfall 558088).

tree.general: Plan and check a radio telemetry network of field sensors, relays and base stations, and inspect the sensor data it delivers
tree.specific: Use Flood-Net to load the ALERT station/repeater dataset, inspect repeater pass ranges, validate radio paths with elevation profile and link budget, find orphaned stations, clashing and ghost addresses, and plot ARRO CSV exports

features.name: Terrain path profile with line of sight and Fresnel zone
features.general: Pick a link between two places on a map, sample the terrain along it, draw the ground with earth curvature, the line of sight and the clearance zone, flag where it is blocked, then change the heights and redraw
features.specific: Click a radio path on the Stations map; the Radio path card draws the elevation profile with the 60% Fresnel ellipse and gives Obstructed/clear, fade margin and the obstructions list; edit TX power, antenna heights or frequency, Flip direction, Copy a summary / Copy for a report / save as PNG
steps: Click a radio path (or draw a Line) on the map
Wait for terrain sampling; read Obstructed/clear, fade margin and obstructions
Edit antenna heights, TX power or frequency to redraw
Flip direction
Copy a summary or a report, or save the chart as PNG
serves_tasks: Draw the terrain profile and line of sight between two linked sites
Try design changes and see how the margin responds
Share the result of a link check

features.name: Two-ended link budget with switchable propagation model
features.general: Set two endpoints (known sites or arbitrary map points), give per-end equipment parameters, choose a propagation model and environment settings, and read a margin verdict with its working
features.specific: Link budget card: arm end A/B and pick a station pin or empty ground (a hypothetical site); per-end TX power, antenna gain and height, line loss and RX threshold; Propagation settings (Model Field-calibrated vs Land cover P.2108, Ground, radio climate, refractivity, permittivity, conductivity, polarization, variability mode, % situations); the result is a fade margin in dB with a Good/Poor verdict
steps: Clear both ends or tick Pick two points on the map
Arm end A and click a station pin
Click empty ground (or another station) for end B
Open Propagation settings and switch the Model or other parameters
Read the fade margin verdict and Show the working
serves_tasks: Check the margin between a real site and a hypothetical new site
Compare propagation models for the same link

steps: Drag the Link distance slider
Read the counts and the amber 'linked to nothing' pins
Press a repeater on the map
Press Show its row to expand its details
serves_tasks: Find relays that are isolated at a chosen link distance
Inspect one relay's coverage and see which field sites it serves

steps: Sort by a column heading
Open a repeater row
Read the stations served and the linked repeaters
Jump to the Stations tab or the map
serves_tasks: Inspect one relay's coverage and see which field sites it serves

features.name: Station map with linked popup and relay panel
features.general: Select a site from a list or a map pin; the map zooms and draws its links, a popup shows its details and nearby gauges within an adjustable radius, and a side panel lists the relays that hear it
features.specific: Stations table row or pin → popup (owner, health, river gauges, Rain within N km slider with ARRO/Flood-Net plot links, Stn #, position, AlertIDs) + Repeaters listening panel + Station details form
steps: Click a station row or pin
Read the popup and the Repeaters listening panel
Drag the Rain within radius slider
Close the popup or Clear the selection
serves_tasks: Open one site to see its details, the relays that hear it and the gauges nearby

features.name: Faceted station filter linked to the map
features.general: Filter a large inventory by free-text or ID ranges and by grouped facets, including 'missing data' facets, with the matches highlighted on the map and counted
features.specific: Stations › Filters: search names, Stn # or AlertIDs (ranges like 4021-4025); Station type checkboxes with counts; Sensor type, Radio network, Owner, Region, Gauge, Basin & council; Data completeness (Position, ALERT address = No address on file, Enabled only)
steps: Open Filters
Expand a facet group
Choose a value (e.g. No address on file)
Read the match count and the highlighted pins
Clear or Clear & zoom out

features.name: Address bit-flip ghost finder
features.general: Enter a numeric identifier, generate the variants that differ from it by N bits, and match each against the inventory to see which other site, sensor and relays a corrupted reading could be wrongly attributed to
features.specific: ALERT › Bit Flipper: ALERT decimal address, Bits to flip, Show only matched addresses, Filter by sensor; the table gives binary, matched station, sensor, Sensor ID and Repeater(s) that pass it, with an Open ARRO graph link and a map
steps: Type an ALERT address
Set Bits to flip
Tick Show only matched addresses
Filter by sensor or open the ARRO graph
serves_tasks: Diagnose misreported (ghost) readings by listing the identifiers one bit-error away from a given one and who holds them

features.name: Address-space wheel and grid
features.general: Show a whole numeric ID space as a radial wheel and a 100-per-row grid, coloured by in use / free / set aside / clash and by relay coverage; press a cell to look it up and filter to it
features.specific: ALERT IDs tab: summary (Orphaned: 691), Show hub selector, All addresses wheel (outer ring = address, middle = repeaters, inner = blocks), Address grid with an Address box; pressing a cell (5547, held by two stations) marks it and puts it in the filter
steps: Choose the hub or network in Show
Point at the wheel or grid to read ownership
Press a cell or type an address
Use the marked address as the page filter
serves_tasks: Count the field sites that no relay covers
Look up who holds a given identifier and spot clashes

features.name: CSV time-series import with continuity filtering
features.general: Drop sensor CSV exports into the browser, auto-link them to their site, run a spike/continuity filter alongside the raw data, and switch between raw, filtered or both, with the rejected points marked
features.specific: Data › Plots: Choose files… / Demo data; each import card shows kept / removed / repeats, a 'reads as' type, line, axis, solo, fit; Filters panel with the 3-5-7 continuity test (step sizes), Correct rollovers; Series Raw/Filtered/Both; Mark 357 ×, range, rise, fall, quality, repeats, rollovers
steps: Choose files… (one or several CSVs)
Read the kept / removed counts per import
Switch Series between Raw, Filtered and Both
Adjust the filter steps or toggles
Solo or hide individual imports
serves_tasks: Import a logger export and chart it with automatic quality filtering
Overlay a second sensor and isolate it

features.name: Interactive time-series chart with drag modes and export
features.general: Chart time series with value, increment or rate views, quick time windows, a chosen drag behaviour (pan, box zoom, ruler and more), axis control and export of the kept data or the image
features.specific: Plots toolbar: Reading Value/Increment/Rate/h, Style Line/Step/Points, Vertical axis Auto/Kept/Zero/Fixed, Window All/24h/7d/30d/90d, Drag does Pan/Box zoom/Horizontal/Vertical/Select/Draw/Ruler, Export Kept CSV / All + verdict CSV / SVG / PNG
steps: Choose a Reading mode and Window
Pick a Drag mode (Box zoom or Ruler) and drag on the chart
Read the hover readout or the ruler rate
Export Kept CSV, SVG or PNG
serves_tasks: Change how the series is shown and zoom into an event
Measure a rate between two points on the chart
